domain: Political Economy / Labor Relations / Debt Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of a deep-sea mining operation where workers operate under debt contracts with compounding obligations. The narrative demonstrates how formal contractual symmetry ('risk-sharing') masks structural extraction through unilateral condition-setting, information asymmetry, and exit cost manipulation.

key_entities: The Consortium (capital provider, contract administrator, equipment owner)
Salvagers (exit community with exclusionary survival code)
Cristina (fugitive performing class signals to access black markets)
key_tensions: Formal contract symmetry vs structural extraction asymmetry
Objective metrics (quotas, debt calculations) vs unilateral condition control
Exit as liberation vs exit as abandonment (Salvager code vs Miner solidarity)
key_mechanisms: Debt compounding through uncontrollable variable costs (equipment rental, penalties, environmental conditions)
Quota rigidity despite observable condition deterioration (nodule density, equipment failure, current surges)
Surface Trust performance (class signaling granting system access without verification)
Salvager code enforcement (exile of those attempting cross-boundary coordination)
absences: Any mechanism for workers to contest condition measurements or quota calculations
Collective bargaining infrastructure or third-party arbitration

omegas.description: At what cost differential does credential verification become cheaper than trust-signal risk? Cristina's arbitrage suggests threshold exists but narrative provides no measurement.
omegas.source: Deferred axis class_signal_arbitrage + Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory)

omegas.description: Would cross-boundary coordination (Miners + Salvagers) structurally improve survival odds, or does Salvager code correctly identify it as fatal compromise? Dao's death is one data point, not proof.
omegas.source: Deferred axis exclusionary_exit_code + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: Why is there no third-party arbitration or metric contestation mechanism? Is this a design choice (snare) or an infrastructure absence (piton)? Narrative shows the absence but not its origin.

Is nodule density decline a natural depletion (mountain) or extraction-induced degradation (piton of prior extraction)? Affects whether unilateral_condition_control is responding to exogenous shock or managing self-created scarcity.
omegas.source: F03 (Hasty Generalization) — environmental condition treated as exogenous without evidence

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: Environmental condition deterioration (nodule density decline, current surges, equipment failure rate increase) treated as exogenous mountain without examining whether these are extraction-induced or management-controlled variables. If Consortium controls maintenance schedules or extraction intensity, condition deterioration may be endogenous piton rather than exogenous constraint. Generated omega_condition_deterioration_cause to bound this uncertainty.
